title: Naked single
subtitle: The last digit in the ring

screens.text: In lesson 4, a digit had only one cell left. Now it is the other way round: a cell has only one digit left, because its row, column and box rule out all the others. That is called a naked single: the last digit sits alone in the ring, plain to see. Tap the marked cell.
screens.praise: Good. Let's find out which digit this cell can be.

wrong.text: That is a different cell. Tap the marked cell.

screens.text: To mark the ring, you need Cross Out mode. Tap the mode switch.
screens.praise: Good. You are in Cross Out mode.

screens.text: First the row. A row holds each digit only once, so this cell cannot be any digit the row already has. Cross out each of them. The marked cells show where they are.
